trial_court: LVII Addl. CMM, Bangalore, CC.No.55706 of 2014
case_name: Mrs. Priya Vargheese vs Aged About 40 Years

parties.respondent_defendant: Aged about 48 years, Complainant (W/o. Mr. Sukumar)

facts_of_case: The Respondent filed a Complaint against the Appellant alleging that she was her neighbourer and had paid an amount of Rs.20,75,000/- to the Appellant. The Appellant had also collected a sum of Rs.2,00,000/- from her husband but failed to repay it as agreed.

legal_principles.principle: The accused must show material evidence to support their defence.
legal_principles.held: But no any material insupport of such contentions are coming forth from the side of the Accused.

legal_principles.principle: The accused must demonstrate a genuine business transaction to justify the issuance of cheques.
legal_principles.held: Though the Complainant admits that she and the Accused have entered into a business of Hallow Bricks, but the Accused has not produced any material to show that, either she has given/issued ExP1−Cheque in the course of the said business transaction or the Complainant has taken Ex.P.1− Cheque from her, under the said business transaction.

outcome.final_order: The trial court convicted the Appellant for the offence punishable under Sec. 138 of NI Act and sentenced her to pay fine of Rs.5,000/- in default to undergo Simple Imprisonment for a period of three months.

use_for_drafting: drafting a complaint under section 138 of the NI Act
appealing a conviction for cheque bounce
understanding the criminal procedure code in India
